TMR 2DN00 quantities of interest: 'Surface pressure coefficient (Cp) vs. x/c (for alpha = 0, 10, 15)'

a0_1_parameters.note: No experimental skin-friction data exist for this case; Cf is computed but cannot be validated.

a0_1_parameters.locator: TMR 2DN00: farfield in the provided grids is 'almost 500 chords away'
a0_1_parameters.note: If a nearer farfield is used, the point-vortex correction of Thomas and Salas (AIAA J 24(7):1074-1080, 1986) is required.

NOT the standard blunt-trailing-edge NACA 0012. Built by extending the exact formula to x=1.008930411365 (sharp TE) then scaling by that factor. Max thickness 11.894 percent of the scaled chord. The prior case file said only 'NACA 0012 (analytic section)', which would have produced the wrong geometry.

a0_2_parameters.locator: Derived from the reported pair (1750 rpm, Mtip 0.612): Mtip scales linearly with rpm, so Mtip(1250) = 0.612 * 1250/1750 = 0.437

amendments.what_changed: Two parameters recorded as MISSING on 2026-09-19 were recovered, and the experimental uncertainty recorded as MISSING for A0.1 is now quantified.
amendments.how: The archived TMR grids page lists the grid and data file paths under NACA0012_grids/ and NACA0012_validation/. Those paths were fetched through the same Internet Archive snapshot route used for the case page. The live domain is still dead; nothing was recovered from it.

items.detail: The full nested C-grid family was recovered. Levels 113x33, 225x65 and 449x129 give a systematic refinement ratio of exactly 2 in each direction, which is what the grid-convergence procedure needs.
items.consequence: The 2026-09-19 statement that results would not be comparable to TMR's published per-grid CFD is WITHDRAWN. The study now runs on the same grid family as the published results.

items.detail: TMR's own curated digitisation of Ladson NASA TM 4074 was recovered: header states Re = 6 million, transition tripped, M = 0.15, which is exactly the case condition. It carries three trip conditions (80, 120 and 180 grit).
items.note: These are TMR's curated data files, not an independent digitisation of the Ladson report by this project. The primary report itself was separately retrieved and hashed (see sources A0.1-LADSON below) so the chain back to the measurement is traceable.

items.detail: The three trip conditions are repeat measurements of the same nominal condition, so their spread is a usable experimental uncertainty. Adjusted to a common angle of 10.12 degrees using the local lift-curve slope of 0.10077 per degree measured from the same dataset: 80 grit 1.07070, 120 grit 1.07952, 180 grit 1.07485. Mean 1.07502, sample standard deviation 0.00441 (0.41 percent).
items.limitation: This captures trip-condition repeatability only. It does not include wall interference, angle-of-attack calibration or any other systematic tunnel effect, so it is a LOWER BOUND on the true experimental uncertainty and the validation statement it supports is correspondingly weak.
